children: Indian government bonds are set for a selloff in early trading on Thursday, tracking a sharp spike in US Treasury yields and oil prices that have further cemented bets that the local central bank may turn hawkish at its next monetary policy meeting.
The benchmark 6.94% 2036 bond yield is expected to trade between 7.05% and 7.10%, according to a trader with a primary dealership, after ending at 7.0447% on Wednesday.

"Whatever little bullishness we had seen in the initial part of the week has completely reversed now, and we are in for a fresh round of selloff, and for now 7.10% seems to be an upside support," the trader said.
US Treasury yields surged after a stronger-than-expected purchasing managers' report ignited fresh inflation fears.
The 10-year Treasury yield rose to its highest level since July 2007.
Oil prices ended higher on Wednesday after Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian vowed he will never surrender, a day after US President Donald Trump warned he could "annihilate" Iran.
The benchmark Brent crude contract, however, eased slightly in Asian hours, as Iran said it remained open to diplomacy to end the Iran war.

India, which imports roughly 90% of its crude oil needs, is particularly exposed to swings in global oil prices, with elevated oil prices and a weak monsoon raising inflation concerns and expectations of an interest rate hike in the next two weeks.

Policy tightening bets in India have hardened after August retail inflation stood at 4.82% and the Federal Reserve raised interest rates by 25 basis points last week, which was its first such move since 2023.
The Reserve Bank of India's monetary policy decision is due on October 7, with most market participants now moving toward a repo rate hike.
Overnight indexed swap rates are expected to spike in line with bond yields.
The one-year (INR1YMIBROIS=CC) rate ended at 6.10%, the two-year (INR2YMIBROIS=CC) rate closed at 6.2950%, and the five-year (INR5YMIBROIS=CC) rate moved 3 bps higher to settle at 6.55%.
